title: Compatibility Sentinel & Provider Pin Registry for Private VPC Upgrades
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a centralized compatibility sentinel and provider pin registry to govern Terraform module and provider upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket covers the schema, automated checks, rollout gates, and runbook updates needed to reduce upgrade regressions and enable safe, auditable upgrades across customer VPC stacks.
background: Over the last year we've seen several Private VPC upgrades that required manual pin rollbacks due to subtle provider behavior changes (provider providerX breaking resource lifecycle; module v2->v3 indentation of variables). Current pinning rules are scattered across repo-level files and docs, which makes coordinated upgrades slow and risky for enterprise customers. Existing tickets (ENG-21045, ENG-17203) outlined provider pinning guidance but lacked an automation + registry to enforce it.
goals: 1) Define a machine-readable provider/module compatibility catalog (registry) for Private deployments. 2) Implement a Compatibility Sentinel service that validates proposed TF plans and module upgrades against the registry. 3) Automate pin updates with safe gate checks and generate upgrade playbooks per customer. 4) Integrate sentinel checks into CI/CD and the Private upgrade pipeline.
non_goals: - Rewriting existing Terraform modules. - Forcing automatic upgrades without human approval. - Covering hosted (non-VPC) product in this ticket.
technical_design_summary: The registry is a small datastore (YAML/JSON files stored in infra-repo and mirrored in S3) with entries for provider versions, module variants, known incompatibilities, and recommended mitigations. The Compatibility Sentinel will be a lightweight service (Go) that: 1) fetches registry snapshot, 2) inspects proposed module/provider changes from a TF plan, 3) matches against compatibility rules, and 4) emits advisory/deny results. CI hook and Private controller will interpret results and surface an actionable checklist. Registry schema includes fields: id, component (module|provider), supported_versions, blocked_versions, min_required_version_for_features, notes, mitigation_link. All code must be auditable and signed in the release branch.
proposed_pinning_policy: - Providers: allow a patch-level range pinned by default (e.g., ~> 3.2.0) for lowest friction; major upgrades must be explicit and go through sentinel approval. - Modules: pin exact module ref for production customers; allow floating refs for canary clusters. - Registry entries must include rationale and a signed approval from infra owners to unlock a blocked range.
automation_work_items: Design registry schema and JSON/YAML format
Implement registry authoring CLI (validate + sign entries)
Build Compatibility Sentinel service with plan analyzer
Add CI hook to run sentinel on PRs touching TF manifests
Integrate sentinel into Private upgrade controller to gate automated upgrades
migration_steps: Export current repo-level provider pins into registry draft
Run a discovery job across customer stacks to baseline current provider/module versions
Authors review and sign initial registry entries for critical providers
Enable sentinel in monitoring-only mode for 2 weeks to collect false positives
Switch sentinel to advisory mode in staging clusters and iterate policies
Enforce sentinel deny mode for production private upgrades once confidence is high
verification_checks: CI: sentinel returns PASS/ADVISORY/DENY with clear reason code
E2E: apply/plan on staging customer stack with sentinel enabled (no unexpected denies)
Smoke: upgrade a canary customer with automated playbook and verify no resource drift
Audit: registry changes require signed approval and are traceable in Git history
rollout_strategy: Staggered rollout: 1) internal infra repos (week 1), 2) staging customer clusters (weeks 2-3), 3) 5% of production private clusters with canary tags (week 4), 4) broad production enforcement (week 6). Provide a scheduled freeze window for pinned major upgrades and clear communication to Customer Success two weeks in advance.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: sentinel_deny_rate by customer and provider
Alerts: >5 denies/hour for production customers; registry signature mismatch; sentinel crashloop
rollback_plan: If sentinel enforcement causes widespread failures: 1) flip enforcement to advisory, 2) revert recent registry entries via signed revert PR, 3) queued upgrades are paused, 4) execute targeted manual rollback for impacted clusters using the generated playbook, 5) postmortem and remediation tasks assigned.
notes: We should coordinate with Security for the signing key lifecycle (KMS/HSM).
Consider a small web UI for registry browsing and reasoned approval flow for infra owners.
Keep initial registry scope limited to providers and core infra modules (networking, storage, compute).
Plan a migration week with Customer Success for high-risk enterprise tenants.
